Parent #1926 / #1645 (SC-10 fault injection; SC-03/06 anti-continuity). Scoped child landing the first deterministic browser fault element and the route-flip cursor fence.

## Requirements: Deterministic high-volume delivery and no pseudo-continuity across a route change

### Problem

The staging fault matrix has no browser-level high-volume witness: nothing submits a burst large enough to cross many frames and queues and then checks the parser's buffer for a hole or a duplicate. Separately, the transport-swap tests pin swap ordering but never assert what happens to the parser-applied cursor when the route changes; carrying it across transports would report synchronization nobody proved.

### Scope

- A 5k-line numbered burst over **both** Relay and P2P: the echoed command must not match the number pattern; readiness waits for the last numbered line (proof that every earlier byte was applied); the check asserts no duplicate anywhere retained and no missing line in the tail window.
- Poll the buffer tail while streaming so the witness does not block the page's WebSocket drain; read the full buffer once after completion.
- A unit test: P2P→Relay flip revokes `terminalAppliedSnapshot`, and a late parser callback from the old binding cannot revive it.
- Register the new canonical spec in the E2E migration-parity inventory (declared count + approved post-migration list).
- No runtime behavior change.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 A 5k numbered burst reaches the xterm parser over Relay and P2P with zero duplicated lines and zero missing lines in the retained tail window, deterministically at the exact PR head SHA.
- [ ] SC-02 A P2P→Relay flip revokes the parser-applied cursor; a late callback bound to the old subscription cannot revive it.
- [ ] SC-03 Exact PR HEAD Quality / E2E / Case Smoke / trusted Acceptance, and exact merge-SHA Quality / E2E / Cases / Orchestrator Pass.
